title: Local Gauge Slices and Faddeev–Popov Jacobians

items.title: Finite-dimensional gauge slices and Faddeev–Popov operators
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; item readiness is recorded separately. The planned Singer theorem has no carrier and remains explicitly escalated in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Fix a compact noncommutative finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$, whose Lie algebra is $\mathfrak g=T_eG$ with bracket transported from left-invariant vector fields. Let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal bundle: the right action is smooth, free and transitive on each fibre, and each point has a local equivariant principal chart. Let $H\subset TP$ be a supplied smooth right-invariant horizontal complement to $VP=\ker(d\pi)$, and write $v$ for projection onto $VP$ along $H$. For $Z\in\mathfrak g$, the fundamental vertical vector is $Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp_G(tZ)$. The principal connection form $\omega$ is a smooth $\mathfrak g$-valued one-form satisfying $\omega(Z_P)=Z$, $\ker\omega=H$, and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$, where $\operatorname{Ad}_g=d(C_g)_e$ and $C_g(h)=ghg^{-1}$. In a local section $s:U\to P$ (a smooth map with $\pi\circ s=\operatorname{id}_U$), the potential $A=s^*\omega$ changes under a section change $s'=su$, for smooth $u:U\to G$, by $A'=\operatorname{Ad}_{u^{-1}}A+\theta_L(u)$, where $\theta_L(u)=u^*\theta_L$, $(\theta_L)_g=d(L_{g^{-1}})_g$, and $L_g(h)=gh$. The full gauge group consists of smooth diffeomorphisms $\Phi:P\to P$ satisfying $\pi\circ\Phi=\pi$ and $\Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g$; this definition gives it no finite-dimensional Lie-group structure.

A **finite-dimensional regulated gauge-slice datum** consists of integers $1\le k\le n$; a finite-dimensional Lie group $K$ of dimension $k$, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak k:=T_eK$ and bracket transported from left-invariant vector fields; a chosen smooth positive left-invariant density $\mu_K$, meaning $(L_h^K)^*\mu_K=\mu_K$ for $L_h^K(g)=hg$; a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $X$ of dimension $n$ with a chosen smooth positive density $\mu_X$; and a smooth right action $\alpha:X\times K\to X$, written $x\cdot g$, with $x\cdot e=x$ and $(x\cdot g)\cdot h=x\cdot(gh)$. A smooth positive density on an $m$-manifold has coordinate form $\rho(x)|dx^1\cdots dx^m|$ with smooth $\rho>0$, and transforms by the absolute coordinate Jacobian. The group $K$ and its action on $X$ are separate regulator data. They are not identified with the full gauge group or the full space of connections unless a particular finite model explicitly constructs such an action and verifies that it preserves $X$.

Choose an embedded smooth submanifold $S\subset X$ of codimension $k$, a smooth positive density $\mu_S$, and an open neighborhood $U\subset X$ of a point $s\in S$. Embedded means that near each point of $S$, a smooth chart on $X$ identifies $S$ with $\mathbb R^{n-k}\times\{0\}$. A **gauge condition** on $U$ is a smooth map $\chi:U\to\mathbb R^k$ such that $U\cap S=\chi^{-1}(0)$ and, for every $s'\in U\cap S$, $d\chi_{s'}$ is surjective with kernel $T_{s'}S$. For every $x\in U$, the **infinitesimal orbit map** is $R_x:=d(\alpha_x)_e:\mathfrak k\to T_xX$, where $\alpha_x(g)=x\cdot g$; call its kernel the infinitesimal stabilizer at $x$. The **Faddeev–Popov operator** at $x$ is the ordinary linear map $M_x:=d\chi_x\circ R_x:\mathfrak k\to\mathbb R^k$. At a slice point $s'\in U\cap S$, call the condition **transverse** when $M_{s'}$ is an isomorphism. Choose a positive density $\nu$ on $\mathfrak k$ equal to $(\mu_K)_e$, and the standard positive density $\lambda$ on $\mathbb R^k$. For every $x\in U$, the finite-dimensional Faddeev–Popov Jacobian $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x)$ is the nonnegative density ratio defined by $M_x^*\lambda=\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x)\nu$; in chosen bases it is $|\det M_x|$, and it is zero when $M_x$ is singular.

This datum defines only finite-dimensional Jacobians and local coordinate slices. It neither defines a determinant of an infinite-dimensional operator nor constructs a functional measure or a continuum path integral. A finite-mode or lattice application must supply the regulator manifold $X$, the finite-dimensional group $K$, their smooth action, and the domains and densities above.

items.title: Local Faddeev–Popov slice Jacobian and orbit-intersection count
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; item readiness is recorded separately. The planned Singer theorem has no carrier and remains explicitly escalated in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and let $(X,K,\alpha,S,\chi,\mu_X,\mu_K,\mu_S)$ be finite-dimensional regulated gauge-slice data as defined above, with $\dim X=n$, $\dim K=k$, $1\le k\le n$, and $s_0\in S\cap U$. Thus $K$ acts smoothly on the right, $S$ is an embedded codimension-$k$ submanifold, $\chi:U\to\mathbb R^k$ is a smooth defining submersion with $\ker d\chi_s=T_sS$, and the Faddeev–Popov operator is $M_s=d\chi_s\circ R_s$. Suppose $M_{s_0}$ is an isomorphism. For $\Psi(g,s)=s\cdot g$, there are neighborhoods $V$ of the identity in $K$, $W$ of $s_0$ in $S$, and $O$ of $s_0$ in $X$ such that $\Psi:V\times W\to O$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism. Consequently, each $x\in O$ has exactly one representation $x=s\cdot g$ with $(g,s)\in V\times W$. In particular, if $s,s'\in W$ and $g\in V$ satisfy $s'=s\cdot g$, then $g=e$ and $s'=s$. This local uniqueness does not assert that every orbit in $X$ meets $W$, or exclude further intersections related by group elements outside $V$.

Fix group coordinates $\xi$ near the identity, slice coordinates $z$ near $s_0$, and adapted target coordinates $(y,z)=(\chi,z)$ near $s_0$. Write the densities there as $\mu_K=\rho_K(\xi)|d\xi|$, $\mu_S=\rho_S(z)|dz|$, and $\mu_X=\rho_X(y,z)|dy\,dz|$. The positive Jacobian $J_\Psi$ defined by $\Psi^*\mu_X=J_\Psi(\mu_K\otimes\mu_S)$ satisfies

$$
J_\Psi(e,s_0)=\frac{\rho_X(0,z_0)}{\rho_S(z_0)}\,\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(s_0),
$$

where $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}$ uses the density $(\mu_K)_e$ and the standard density on $\mathbb R^k$. Thus, when the target and slice densities are normalized so that $\rho_X(0,z_0)=\rho_S(z_0)$, the ordinary finite-dimensional orbit-to-slice Jacobian is exactly $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(s_0)$. For every compactly supported Riemann-integrable function $f:O\to\mathbb R$, the local change-of-variables identity is
$$
\int_O f\,d\mu_X=\int_{V\times W}(f\circ\Psi)J_\Psi\,d\mu_K\,d\mu_S.
$$

For the exact multiplicity statement, fix $x\in X$ and a relatively compact open set $\Gamma\subset K$ such that $x\cdot\overline{\Gamma}\subset U$. Let $F_x(g)=\chi(x\cdot g)$. Let $r\ge 0$ be finite, and suppose $F_x$ has exactly $r$ zeros $g_1,\ldots,g_r$ in the support of a smooth function $\varphi$ compactly supported in $\Gamma$, each $M_{x\cdot g_i}$ is invertible, and the slice points $s_i=x\cdot g_i$ are distinct. Choose a nonnegative $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^k)$, supported in a ball $B_C(0)$ of finite radius $C>0$, with integral $1$, and set $\eta_\epsilon(y)=\epsilon^{-k}\eta(y/\epsilon)$. Then

$$
\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\int_\Gamma \varphi(g)\,\eta_\epsilon(F_x(g))\,\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x\cdot g)\,d\mu_K(g)=\sum_{i=1}^r\varphi(g_i).
$$

In particular, if $\varphi=1$ near the zeros, this finite-regulator expression counts the $r$ distinct transverse intersections exactly. The theorem asserts only a local chart and this finite-dimensional multiplicity formula; it gives no global gauge section, functional determinant, or continuum path-integral measure.

items.title: Existence of a smooth principal connection on a compact SU(N) bundle
items.design_state: Step 1 intermediate result authored with a complete local partition-of-unity proof; current dependency interfaces and readiness are recorded in batch-3 notes.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a nonempty compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, let $N\ge2$, and let $P\to M$ be any smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle. Write $SU(N)=\{g\in M_N(\mathbb C):g^*g=I,\det g=1\}$ and $\mathfrak{su}(N)=\{X\in M_N(\mathbb C):X^*=-X,\operatorname{tr}X=0\}$. Then there exists a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(N)$-valued one-form $\omega$ on $P$ such that, for every $X\in\mathfrak{su}(N)$, its fundamental vertical vector is $X_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp(tX)$, and
$$
\omega(X_P)=X,\qquad R_h^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{h^{-1}}\omega\quad(h\in SU(N)),
$$
where $R_h(p)=ph$ and $\operatorname{Ad}_h(X)=hXh^{-1}$. Such a one-form is a smooth principal connection form; the conclusion does not assert a global trivialization of $P$.

references.title: Karl-Hermann Neeb, Differential Topology of Fiber Bundles (2024)

items.title: Singer obstruction to a global continuous gauge representative
items.design_state: Step 1 continuation authored the full all-bundle S3/S4 theorem and complete local proof. Direct batch-56/57/58 interfaces are inspected and current; the original Singer source remains an attribution-only access limitation recorded in batch-3.coverage.json.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $r\in\{3,4\}$, let $N\ge2$, and let $P\to S^r$ be any smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle, with the standard round metric and orientation on $S^r$. Here $S^r=\{x\in\mathbb R^{r+1}:\|x\|=1\}$, and $SU(N)=\{U\in M_N(\mathbb C):U^*U=I,\det U=1\}$. A principal right bundle means a smooth surjective bundle with free right $SU(N)$ action, locally equivariantly diffeomorphic to $U\times SU(N)$. Write $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ for its Lie algebra, set $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$, using $[pg,z]=[p,gzg^{-1}]$ and $\operatorname{Ad}_g z=gzg^{-1}$. A smooth principal connection is a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(N)$-valued one-form $\omega$ on $P$ with $\omega(\xi_P)=\xi$ for each fundamental vertical vector $\xi_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp(t\xi)$ and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$, where $R_g(p)=pg$. Let $\mathcal A^\infty(P)$ be the affine space of these connections, modeled on $\Omega^1(S^r;\operatorname{ad}P)$, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all derivative seminorms in a fixed finite bundle atlas. Let $\mathcal G^\infty(P)=\Gamma^\infty(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ be the smooth gauge group with pointwise multiplication and its $C^\infty$ section topology. For the Sobolev intermediary choose a smooth reference connection $A_0$ (its existence is also exhibited in the proof), fix any integer $k>r/2+1$, and use $\mathcal A_k(P)=A_0+H^k(T^*S^r\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $\mathcal G_{k+1}(P)=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$, where these Sobolev spaces are completions in the finite-atlas norms from square-integrable derivatives through the indicated order.

Fix $m\in S^r$ and a frame $p_m\in P_m$. Parallel transport around piecewise smooth loops based at $m$, expressed in this frame, gives the holonomy subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. A connection is **irreducible** when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; this condition is unchanged by conjugating the chosen frame. Write $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)\subseteq\mathcal A^\infty(P)$ for this locus. In local sections the right gauge action is $A^u=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$.

Let $Z_N=\{\zeta I_N:\zeta^N=1\}$ be the central subgroup of constant gauge sections and let $\overline{\mathcal G}^\infty(P)=\mathcal G^\infty(P)/Z_N$ with its quotient topology. Give every orbit space below its quotient topology, and define
$$
q_*:\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)\longrightarrow\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)/\overline{\mathcal G}^\infty(P),\qquad q:\mathcal A^\infty(P)\longrightarrow\mathcal A^\infty(P)/\mathcal G^\infty(P)
$$
to be the reduced and full orbit projections. A continuous section of either projection is a continuous right inverse. The natural square

```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P) \arrow[r,hook,"j"] \arrow[d,"q_*"'] & \mathcal A^\infty(P) \arrow[d,"q"] \\
\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)/\overline{\mathcal G}^\infty(P) \arrow[r,"\iota"'] & \mathcal A^\infty(P)/\mathcal G^\infty(P)
\end{tikzcd}
```

commutes, where $j$ is inclusion and $\iota$ sends a reduced orbit to its full orbit. The map $\iota$ identifies its domain with the open subset $q(\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P))$ of the full orbit space.

Neither $q_*$ nor $q$ has a continuous section. Both conclusions hold for every bundle sector, including nontrivial bundles; irreducibility here does not mean that the holonomy equals all of $SU(N)$.

items.title: Translation action with a unit Faddeev–Popov Jacobian
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; item readiness is recorded separately. The planned Singer theorem has no carrier and remains explicitly escalated in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Take $M=\{\star\}$ and
$$G=SU(2):=\{q\in M_2(\mathbb C):q^*q=I_2,\ \det q=1\}$$
with matrix multiplication and Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)=\{Z\in M_2(\mathbb C):Z^*=-Z,\ \operatorname{tr}Z=0\}$. Its elements are exactly $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\-\overline b&\overline a\end{pmatrix}$ with $|a|^2+|b|^2=1$, giving a diffeomorphism with the unit sphere in $\mathbb C^2$; matrix multiplication and inversion are smooth. Thus $G$ is a compact noncommutative finite-dimensional real Lie group, as checked in the Verification. Let $P=SU(2)\to M$ with right multiplication, $H=0$, and $\omega_q(V)=q^{-1}V$ for $V\in T_qSU(2)$; this specifies the principal bundle and connection datum. Choose the independent regulator $X=\mathbb R^2$ with coordinates $(u,v)$ and density $du\,dv$, the additive Lie group $K=(\mathbb R,+)$ with left-invariant density $dt$, and the smooth right action
$$
(u,v)\cdot t=(u+t,v).
$$
Let $S=\{(0,v):v\in\mathbb R\}$, choose $s_0=(0,0)\in S$, and set $U=X$. Let $\chi(u,v)=u$ and give $S$ density $dv$. For every $s=(0,v)\in S$, the Faddeev–Popov operator is $M_s(t)=t$, so $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(s)=1$. The local orbit-to-slice map is $\Psi(t,(0,v))=(t,v)$, with density Jacobian $1$. For $x=(a,b)$, the gauge condition along its orbit is $F_x(t)=a+t$; it has one transverse zero $t_0=-a$, and the slice meets this orbit once. If $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R$ is relatively compact and open with $t_0\in\Gamma$, and $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Gamma)$ has $t_0\in\operatorname{supp}\varphi$, then for every nonnegative compactly supported smooth $\eta$ of integral $1$, the regularized intersection expression tends to $\varphi(t_0)$.

items.title: SO(2) orbit with two slice intersections and a stabilizer at the origin
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; item readiness is recorded separately. The planned Singer theorem has no carrier and remains explicitly escalated in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Take $M=\{\star\}$ and
$$G=SU(2):=\{q\in M_2(\mathbb C):q^*q=I_2,\ \det q=1\}$$
with matrix multiplication and Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)=\{Z\in M_2(\mathbb C):Z^*=-Z,\ \operatorname{tr}Z=0\}$. Its elements are exactly $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\-\overline b&\overline a\end{pmatrix}$ with $|a|^2+|b|^2=1$, giving a diffeomorphism with the unit sphere in $\mathbb C^2$; matrix multiplication and inversion are smooth. Thus $G$ is a compact noncommutative finite-dimensional real Lie group, as checked in the Verification. Let $P=SU(2)\to M$ with right multiplication, $H=0$, and $\omega_q(V)=q^{-1}V$ for $V\in T_qSU(2)$; this specifies the principal bundle and connection datum. Choose the independent regulator $X=\mathbb R^2$ with Lebesgue density. Write $R_\theta=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}\in SO(2)$ for $\theta\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$. Let $K=SO(2)$ with left-invariant density $|d\theta|$, and define the smooth right action
$$
(x,y)\cdot R_\theta=(x\cos\theta+y\sin\theta,\,-x\sin\theta+y\cos\theta).
$$
Take $S=\{(x,0):x\in\mathbb R\}$, choose $s_0=(1,0)\in S$, and set $U=X$. Let $\chi(x,y)=y$ and give $S$ density $dx$. At $s=(r,0)$, the orbit differential in the angle direction is $(0,-r)$, so $M_s(1)=-r$ and $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(s)=|r|$. For $r>0$, the orbit-to-slice map is $\Psi(R_\theta,(r,0))=(r\cos\theta,-r\sin\theta)$, whose coordinate Jacobian at the identity is $r$, agreeing with the Faddeev–Popov density ratio. For a fixed orbit point $x_0=(r,0)$, $r>0$, the gauge function is $F_{x_0}(R_\theta)=-r\sin\theta$. Its two zeros are $\theta=0,\pi$, with distinct slice points $(r,0)$ and $(-r,0)$, and both are transverse. Taking $\Gamma=SO(2)$ and the test function $\varphi=1$, the regularized intersection expression tends to $2$. At the origin the full group stabilizes the point, $M_{(0,0)}=0$, and $F_{(0,0)}$ vanishes on all of $SO(2)$; the theorem's isolated transverse-zero hypotheses fail there.
